title: Consolidation Playbook for LLM Inference Buyers — Platform, Economics, and Risk Signals
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
- This playbook helps field teams and technical buyers decide when to consolidate multiple inference providers into a single platform (Redwood Dedicated/Private/Hosted). It combines commercial signals, technical tradeoffs, a competitive brief, pilot checklist, a short pitch flow, pricing scenarios, a compact case study, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform engineers, CTOs, procurement, and Redwood sales & solution engineers.
- Scope: consolidation decisions where customers evaluate economics, latency SLAs, compliance constraints, and operational overhead across 2–6 inference vendors.

When consolidation makes sense (high-level signals)

1) Economic signal (must):
- Multiple vendors with overlapping workloads producing >$25k/mo combined inference spend AND >20% month-over-month growth in serving volume.
- Fragmentation causes >15% waste from idle reserved capacity or duplicate engineering integrations (measured by time-to-onboard * headcount cost).

2) Operational signal (must):
- Multiple integration points for routing, logging, observability, and access control. If on-call noise (pager incidents tied to inference) has >5 outages per quarter attributable to vendor switching, consolidation is warranted.

3) Performance signal (strong):
- Tight latency SLOs (p95 < 300ms for real-time tasks) and high tail-p50/p95 variance across providers.

4) Compliance/sensitivity signal (optional):
- Data residency, audit log centralization, or KMS/HSM requirements that are harder to guarantee across multiple hosted vendors.

Value thesis for consolidation (how Redwood wins)

- Single control plane: consistent rollout, auditing, and model versioning across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Predictable unit economics: centralized batching, KV cache reuse, and quantization profiles reduce per-token cost by 10–40% depending on workload.
- Operational simplicity: one tracing/alerting contract reduces MTTR by 30–60% in benchmarked accounts.

Competitive brief (short, actionable)

Key competitors considered during consolidation deals:
- Major public LLM API provider A: advantage = breadth of models; drawback = limited private deployment and higher per-token price at scale.
- Inference appliance vendor B: advantage = on-prem control; drawback = heavier ops and slower model updates.
- Open-source orchestrators + self-hosted fleets: advantage = cost control; drawback = engineering lift and brittle upgrades.

How to position Redwood vs. each:
- Vs Provider A: emphasize predictable committed capacity, SLA-backed latency, and transparent batching gains (show sample cost per 1M tokens).
- Vs Appliance B: highlight faster model onboarding (2–4 week vs 8–12 weeks), integrated KMS options, and centralized telemetry across cloud+onprem.
- Vs DIY fleets: call out total cost of ownership (engineering FTEs to keep a reliable inference runtime), and Redwood Optimize recommendations that reduce runtime spend without sacrificing quality.

Competitive matrix (snapshot)

- Attributes: Hosted latency SLA | Private deployment | Batch/caching economics | Rollout tooling | Support for quantized variants | Audit/KMS integr.
- Redwood: Yes | Yes | Strong (10–40%) | Canary + automatic fallback | Yes | KMS/HSM + audit log.
- Provider A: Yes | Partial | Weak | Basic | Limited | Partial.
- Vendor B: No | Yes | Moderate | Manual | Moderate | On-prem HSM only.

Pilot / consolidation checklist (technical + commercial)

Pre-pilot (sales + procurement):
1. Define target routes: pick 1–3 inference routes (e.g., chat API, reranker, and embeddings) that represent 60–80% of traffic and economics.
2. Agree success metrics: cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency, error rate, and MTTR target for incidents.
3. Sign NDA + pilot T&Cs: include data residency and retention terms, sample SLAs for pilot.

Pilot steps (recommended 6–8 weeks):
1. Initial integration (Week 0–1): grant API keys, validate test corpus, and validate model parity on 50 prompts. Owner: SE.
2. Performance baseline (Week 1–2): collect p50/p95/p99 across existing providers for the selected routes. Owner: customer platform + Redwood SRE.
3. Cost modeling (Week 2): run Redwood cost simulator on actual traffic trace (sample 24h) to show batching and cache effects. Owner: Redwood solutions engineering.
4. Canary roll (Week 3–5): route 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic using progressive canary; monitor latency, errors, and semantic drift (sample evals). Use automatic fallback policy for model variants. Owner: customer eng + Redwood SRE.
5. Cutover and validation (Week 6–8): finalize routing, migrate secrets to production KMS, and run a 72-hour soak with monitoring dashboards. Owner: customer platform + Redwood ops.

Success criteria (examples):
- Achieve <=10% cost delta vs expected (accounting for batching savings).
- p95 latency meets agreed SLO within 5%.
- Zero unplanned production rollbacks during 72-hour soak.

Pitch snippets (soundbites for executive/technical audiences)

- Executive: "One inference platform that reduces your per-token spend while giving your security and platform teams a single source of truth for model controls and audits."
- Platform engineer: "Ship consistent model rollouts and get predictable tail latency with built-in KV cache and workload-aware batching — no custom fleet ops."
- CFO: "We convert duplicate reserved spend and fragmented integration overhead into a predictable committed capacity with a clear unit-cost curve."

Pricing guidance (simple scenarios to use in field conversations)

Assumptions: committed monthly capacity, pilot discount, and uplift for private deployments. These are illustrative only; use the pricing simulator for final quotes.

Scenario table (example economics)

- Low-volume consolidation (startup):
  - Current spend: $10k/month across 2 providers
  - Redwood Hosted projected: $9k/mo (5–15% savings after batching)
  - Time to onboard: 1 week (self-serve)

- Mid-market consolidation (product team):
  - Current spend: $65k/month across 3 providers
  - Redwood Dedicated projected: $45k–$52k/mo with a 12-month commit (30% median saving due to batch reuse and KV cache)
  - Recommended contract: 12-month reserved with burst buffer and prioritized support

- Regulated enterprise (finance/healthcare):
  - Current spend: $220k/month across 4 vendors, plus 2 FTEs managing custom orchestration
  - Redwood Private projected: $160k–$175k/mo (includes on-prem package or VPC control plane) + professional services (3–6 weeks)
  - Recommendation: multi-year commit, extended observability retention, and SOC2/ISO annexes

Case study (compact, anonymized)

- Customer: mid-sized e-commerce platform (anonymized: "RetailCo")
- Situation: used three inference vendors for chat, personalization, and recommendations; invoices and quotas were inconsistent; platform team spent 0.6 FTE on integrations.
- Pilot: moved chat + personalization (60% of tokens) to Redwood Dedicated pilot (8-week).
- Outcomes:
  - Cost: 28% lower per-token after batching and unified cache.
  - Latency: p95 improved from 420ms -> 270ms.
  - Ops: On-call alerts attributed to inference dropped 55% in first quarter.
  - ROI: Payback on migration effort within 5 months (including SE hours).

Security FAQ (customer-facing, short answers)

Q: How does Redwood ensure data isolation when we consolidate providers?
A: Customers choose the deployment mode that matches their isolation needs: Hosted with logically separated tenants, Dedicated GPU pools for tenant-level isolation, or Private (VPC/on-prem) where control plane and data paths are within customer-managed networks. Audit logs are centralized and integrate with SIEM via syslog/HTTPS.

Q: What KMS/HSM options are supported for key management?
A: Redwood supports AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-based key wrapping for private deployments. Customer keys can be brought and rotated according to your policy.

Q: Will model artifacts or prompts be stored outside our region?
A: No — for Private and Dedicated customers we support region pinning and model artifact residency controls. Hosted customers can request region-specific contracts where supported.

Q: How do you validate model-change quality during rollouts?
A: We run pre-rollout evals on customer-provided prompt sets and monitor semantic regression metrics (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding-distance drift, and custom acceptance tests). Rollouts default to canary + automatic fallback to prior model variant on quality regressions.

Q: What compliance attestation do you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001, and can share third-party audit evidence under NDA. Private deployments can include custom attestations in contract.

Objections and rebuttals (field-ready)

- "We like best-of-breed model choice across providers."
  - Rebuttal: Redwood maintains a model catalog and supports routing policies to hybridize best-of-breed choices while still providing a single control plane and unified telemetry.

- "We're worried about vendor lock-in."
  - Rebuttal: Redwood supports exportable audit logs, client-side routing adapters, and can run a dual-write pilot during migration to reduce lock-in risk.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE handoff)

- Alerts to configure during pilot:
  1. p95 token latency > SLO + 25% for 5 minutes -> Pager to platform oncall.
  2. Error rate spike > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 3 minutes -> SE triage.
  3. Model quality drift (embedding distance > threshold) -> Data-science review.

- Dashboard essentials:
  - Per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model-variant rollouts, cache hit rate, batching utilization, and cost per 1000 tokens.

Appendix: useful snippets and templates

- Example canary policy (YAML):
  ---
  name: progressive-canary
  steps:
    - traffic: 5%
      duration: 24h
    - traffic: 25%
      duration: 48h
    - traffic: 100%
      duration: 72h
  rollback_on:
    - p95_latency_increase_pct: 15
    - semantic_regression_score: true

- Template success metric table (to share in pilot SOW):
  | metric | baseline | target | owner | acceptance |
  | p95 latency | 420ms | <=300ms | platform eng | pass
  | cost per 1M tokens | $20 | <=$16 | finance | pass
  | inference-related incidents / quarter | 6 | <=2 | platform | pass

- Quick CLI validation example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
